title: Onboarding checklist experiment
task: Design an experiment to test whether an onboarding checklist increases week-1 retention of our note-taking app.

brief.goal: Design a randomised experiment that shows whether an onboarding checklist increases week-1 retention of the note-taking app.
brief.audience: The product and data leads who decide whether to ship the checklist.
brief.assumptions: Week-1 retention is about 30% today. The checklist is built and behind a feature flag. Enough new users sign up each week to fill both groups within a few weeks ([WEEKLY SIGN-UPS]).
brief.outOfScope: Redesigning the onboarding screens; changes to paid acquisition.
brief.doneWhen: All 7 reviewed sections are approved by the Critic, and anything unresolved is listed under Open questions.

sections.name: Hypothesis
sections.guidance: One testable hypothesis with a direction and a null hypothesis.

sections.name: Variables
sections.guidance: Independent, dependent and controlled variables, each with how it is operationalised.

sections.name: Method
sections.guidance: Design (e.g. randomised A/B, within-subjects), procedure step by step, duration.

sections.name: Sample and controls
sections.guidance: Who takes part, how they are recruited and assigned, the control condition, and the sample size with its justification.

sections.name: Measurements
sections.guidance: Each metric with its exact definition, unit, time window and data source.

sections.name: Analysis plan
sections.guidance: Primary test, significance level, power, how missing data and multiple comparisons are handled, and the decision rule.

sections.name: Risks and ethics
sections.guidance: Consent, privacy and data retention, possible harms and how they are mitigated, and stop conditions.

sections.name: Open questions
sections.guidance: Questions raised during the run that no agent could answer. Not reviewed.

spans.why: A run starts with a brief the user approves before anything else happens.
